candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: therapeutic communication, therapeutic relationships, coping/psychosocial support, and professional boundaries.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — therapeutic use of self, communication, and boundaries
candidate.educational_objective: Use self-awareness, purposeful presence, empathy, therapeutic communication, and professional boundaries intentionally to advance the client's therapeutic goals rather than creating a social friendship or withdrawing emotionally.

options.A: Use frequent personal self-disclosure to create a friendship and make the relationship less professionally bounded.
options.B: Remain emotionally detached and avoid reflecting on personal reactions so the nurse's self never enters the interaction.
options.C: Use self-awareness, purposeful presence, empathy, therapeutic communication, and professional boundaries to support the client's therapeutic goals.
options.D: Agree with the client's beliefs and decisions automatically even when doing so conflicts with therapeutic goals or professional judgment.

candidate.rationale: Current Open RN/NCBI mental-health nursing guidance describes the therapeutic nurse-client relationship as a purposeful professional relationship focused on client needs and goals. Effective therapeutic communication includes self-awareness, client-centered active listening and empathy, intentional presence, and maintenance of professional boundaries; personal self-disclosure and boundary blurring are identified as barriers. Therefore C best demonstrates therapeutic use of self. A blurs professional boundaries, B rejects the reflective self-awareness and therapeutic presence needed for the relationship, and D substitutes indiscriminate agreement for therapeutic communication and professional judgment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Therapeutic use of self is intentional, self-aware, client-centered professional engagement using empathy, presence, communication, and boundaries to support client goals; friendship-seeking disclosure, detachment, and boundary blurring are nontherapeutic.
candidate.source_document_title: Therapeutic Communication and the Nurse-Client Relationship, 2nd edition
candidate.source_locator: Chapter 2 > Nurse-Client Relationship: therapeutic relationship is compassionate, supportive, professional, establishes trust/rapport with a specific purpose and supports client goals. Therapeutic Communication/Tips for Effective Therapeutic Communication: establish a goal; be self-aware; be client-centered; provide empathy; use active listening; avoid personal self-disclosure; maintain professional boundaries. Common Barriers: lack of awareness of personal biases/feelings and blurring nurse-client boundaries.

candidate.source_version_date: 2nd edition published November 1, 2025; currentness live-rechecked August 16, 2026
